Name: Default-Deny Inbound Firewall
Description: Stateful inbound filtering that protects unsolicited inbound connections while preserving explicitly authorized services and required connectivity.

Name: Rate Limiting and Flood Protection
Description: Protect against excessive connection attempts, SYN floods, ICMP abuse, UDP floods, and other detectable network-level resource abuse using supported Windows facilities.

Name: Port Scan Detection
Description: Detect suspicious scanning behavior and apply safe, expiring source restrictions where reliable and supported.

Name: Anti-Spoofing and Malformed Packet Filtering
Description: Detect or reject supported spoofed, malformed, or clearly invalid traffic without breaking legitimate fragmentation or network protocols.

Name: Threat-Intelligence IP Blocking
Description: Integrate verified, reputable intelligence sources such as Spamhaus and abuse.ch. Apply high-confidence restrictions only, with freshness, false-positive, and essential-network safeguards.

Name: IPv6 Protection Parity
Description: Ensure appropriate IPv6 monitoring and protection rather than securing only IPv4.

Name: Cloud Metadata Endpoint Protection
Description: Protect access to cloud metadata addresses such as `169.254.169.254` when relevant. Avoid unnecessary system-wide changes on ordinary home PCs.

Name: DNS Rebinding Protection
Description: Detect suspicious DNS responses that could expose local resources. Apply blocking only when supported safely and without breaking legitimate internal-domain resolution.

Name: Untrusted Network Protection
Description: Recognize trusted and untrusted network profiles and apply safer inbound policies on public or unfamiliar Wi-Fi, including compatible Windows sharing controls.

Name: Bluetooth Security Monitoring
Description: Monitor unexpected Bluetooth pairing, connections, and discoverability, applying supported reversible hardening where appropriate.

Name: Honeytokens and Canary Files
Description: Create isolated decoy credentials and files, monitor access, and generate high-severity alerts. Never create functioning credentials or expose real secrets.

Name: Canary DNS and URLs
Description: Implement local canary access monitoring and provide externally reachable canary functionality only when a suitable endpoint actually exists. Never claim off-machine monitoring from a purely local implementation.

Name: Decoy Services and Honeypots
Description: Provide isolated, low-risk decoy listeners or simulated services on unused ports, with event capture, safety restrictions, and optional expiring source bans. Avoid exposing vulnerable real services.

Name: Intrusion Detection
Description: Integrate a Windows-compatible intrusion detection engine or equivalent established detection capability. Support validated detection rules and updates.

Name: Network Metadata and Attack Classification
Description: Collect available network telemetry and correlate relevant events to recognizable attack behaviors and MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

Name: Connection and DNS Journal
Description: Record supported per-process network connections and DNS observations. Detect unusual outbound destinations, tunneling indicators, and first-time connection behavior.

Name: ARP Spoofing Alerts
Description: Detect suspicious ARP changes and possible local-network interception attempts.

Name: Rogue DHCP and Evil-Twin Wi-Fi Detection
Description: Detect suspicious DHCP or wireless-network changes using telemetry actually available from Windows and the installed wireless adapter.

Name: Listening Port and Attack-Surface Monitor
Description: Identify listening ports and services. Alert when new services unexpectedly begin accepting connections.

Name: New LAN Device Alerts
Description: Observe and report newly discovered local-network devices using passive telemetry and safe network discovery where enabled.

Name: Unsafe Network Alerts
Description: Warn when connected to open, obsolete, or otherwise weakly secured wireless networks.

Name: Suspicious SMTP Activity
Description: Identify unexpected outbound SMTP activity from applications not normally associated with email transmission.

Name: Remote-Access Monitoring
Description: Detect newly enabled or installed remote-management services, including RDP, VNC, and recognizable remote-support applications.

Name: Clock Drift Monitoring
Description: Detect material system clock drift or suspicious time changes that could affect security verification and logs.

Name: Persistence and Software Installation Monitoring
Description: Track new services, scheduled tasks, startup entries, browser extensions where accessible, and installed software or drivers.

Name: Rootkit and Kernel Driver Monitoring
Description: Monitor suspicious driver installation and available Windows kernel-integrity indicators using supported APIs and established tools where bundled.

Name: Privilege Escalation Monitoring
Description: Alert on new administrator accounts, unexpected privilege changes, security-policy changes, and suspicious elevation events.

Name: Camera and Microphone Access Alerts
Description: Use supported Windows privacy and device-access telemetry to identify unexpected camera or microphone activity.

Name: Cryptominer and Resource-Abuse Detection
Description: Detect patterns of suspicious sustained resource consumption, mining-related behavior, and unauthorized compute activity.

Name: Runtime and System Activity Monitoring
Description: Use Windows Event Log, ETW, security auditing, and optionally bundled supported monitoring components to observe relevant runtime activity.

Name: Browser Credential and Session Protection
Description: Detect suspicious access to browser credential and session storage using available filesystem and process telemetry without reading or transmitting actual secrets unnecessarily.

Name: Clipboard Hijacking Detection
Description: Detect supported indicators of malicious clipboard modification, including unexpected changes to copied payment or cryptocurrency addresses. Preserve clipboard privacy.

Name: System Trust Configuration Monitoring
Description: Watch trusted root certificates, proxy settings, hosts-file changes, and network or DNS configuration tampering.

Name: Bulk-Copy and Exfiltration Alerts
Description: Detect suspicious high-volume copying or movement of protected files where sufficient telemetry exists. Do not falsely claim complete visibility into encrypted cloud transfers.

Name: File and Binary Integrity Monitoring
Description: Monitor selected system files, application binaries, startup configuration, and critical security settings. Alert on unexpected modifications.

Name: Suspicious Execution Monitoring
Description: Detect relevant abuse patterns involving PowerShell, WMI, script hosts, suspicious command lines, process relationships, user-writable execution paths, disguised executables, and other detectable malicious execution behavior.

Name: Boot-Chain Integrity Monitoring
Description: Monitor available Secure Boot, TPM, boot-configuration, and startup-integrity indicators.

Name: Keylogger and Input-Hook Detection
Description: Detect suspicious input-monitoring behavior where supported. Clearly disclose any Windows telemetry limitations.

Name: Package and Software Source Integrity
Description: Monitor relevant software repositories, trusted publishers, package-source configuration, and certificate or update-source changes.

Name: Container Exposure Audit
Description: Check locally installed container platforms, where present, for exposed management interfaces, unsafe network publishing, and insecure permissions. Skip cleanly if none are installed.

Name: Brute-Force Protection
Description: Detect repeated failed login attempts for supported local and remote services and apply safe restrictions where feasible, with trusted-access exclusions.

Name: SSH Hardening Audit
Description: Audit OpenSSH configuration when installed, including root-equivalent access, password authentication, key security, and exposed services. Report-only by default.

Name: Credential Breach Checking
Description: Provide an optional privacy-preserving credential breach-checking feature, using k-anonymity where supported. Remain idle without user-provided inputs; never upload plaintext passwords.

Name: Account Security Audit
Description: Identify stale local accounts, insecure authentication policies, unexpected administrator access, and other detectable account-security weaknesses.

Name: Login and Privilege-Use Alerts
Description: Monitor supported local logins, remote logins, failed authentication, and administrator elevation.

Name: Windows Security Hardening Audit
Description: Audit available protections such as ASLR, DEP, Secure Boot, TPM, Defender status, firewall profiles, encryption, password policy, device security, insecure permissions, and screen-lock configuration.

Name: Reversible Automatic Hardening
Description: Apply a narrow set of safe, validated Windows security improvements. Include appropriate AutoRun/AutoPlay, legacy-protocol, and built-in security checks. Every modification requires rollback support.

Name: Browser Security Audit
Description: Inspect supported browsers for detectable risky configuration, untrusted extensions, and missing security settings without unnecessarily collecting browsing history.

Name: External Exposure Assessment
Description: Report local exposure and optionally query available public exposure intelligence. Clearly distinguish internal observations from genuine externally verified scans.

Name: Secrets Hygiene Scanner
Description: Detect likely exposed credentials, private keys, and tokens in user-authorized files and development directories. Protect scan results and avoid retaining plaintext secrets.

Name: Remote Feature and Hardware Security Audit
Description: Audit supported management and remote-access capabilities such as Wake-on-LAN, Intel AMT where present, remote assistance, DMA-related settings, and exposed administrative interfaces.

Name: Updates and Vulnerability Assessment
Description: Detect missing Windows security updates and known vulnerabilities in identifiable software using verified vulnerability data. Report firmware and BIOS findings only where reliable information exists.

Name: Watchdog Service
Description: Monitor critical application components and safely restart failed services when appropriate.

Name: Dead-Man's Switch
Description: Detect when required protection services or the watchdog stop reporting health.

Name: Privilege Separation
Description: Separate ordinary UI components from privileged firewall management and protected configuration operations.

Name: Hostile Input Handling
Description: Safely parse untrusted filenames, event data, DNS names, logs, and other inputs. Use validation, isolation, fuzz testing, and least-privilege execution.

Name: Verified Security Updates and Feeds
Description: Validate update authenticity and integrity using appropriate signing and verification mechanisms. Reject corrupted or untrusted updates.

Name: Supply-Chain Protection
Description: Pin dependencies, verify build inputs, generate an SBOM, and run vulnerability checks against the application's software dependencies.

Name: Rule Safety Guard
Description: Check active security rules against expected configuration, identify unsafe deviations, and coordinate safe rollback without overwriting legitimate third-party changes.

Name: Alert Pipeline
Description: Provide desktop notifications, severity levels, duplicate suppression, alert history, and summaries. External messaging integrations are optional and must not be required.

Name: Secure Structured Logging
Description: Provide structured logs, retention controls, rotation, compression, bounded storage, and tamper-evident protections where feasible.

Name: Resource Governor
Description: Continuously manage the workload of heavyweight scanners, traffic analysis, and monitoring based on CPU, memory, disk usage, and battery state.

Name: Threat Feed Freshness
Description: Monitor intelligence and detection-rule age. Identify missing, stale, corrupted, or failed updates.

Name: Protected Secrets Storage
Description: Use Windows DPAPI, Credential Manager, or supported system cryptography to protect application secrets and keys.

Name: UI and Privileged Service Access Protection
Description: Restrict administrative operations through proper Windows access control, authenticated IPC, authorization checks, and abuse prevention.

Name: Forensic Snapshot
Description: On selected high-severity events, securely preserve available process, connection, system-state, and recent event evidence.

Name: Security Posture Score
Description: Calculate a transparent 0–100 security score with weighted categories, explanations, data-confidence indicators, and actionable recommendations.

Name: Encrypted Versioned Backups
Description: Provide encrypted, versioned backups with restore verification. Prefer an independently protected destination when available. Clearly explain when backups remain vulnerable because they reside on the same machine.

Name: Offline Recovery Kit
Description: Generate recovery scripts, configuration exports, and printable instructions. Create bootable recovery media only when compatible media, authorized software, and the required Windows components are available.

Name: Resilient Log Export
Description: Support encrypted export and shipping to a configured external destination. Without an external destination, retain bounded local archives and report that off-device protection is not configured.

Name: Automated Regression Tests
Description: Test layer behavior, configuration safety, recovery, rule preservation, and compatibility after software updates.

Name: Quarterly Security Reports
Description: Generate scheduled reports showing security posture trends, detection activity, layer health, major alerts, and recommended improvements.

Name: Firewall Conflict and Shadowing Analysis
Description: Detect duplicate, conflicting, shadowed, ineffective, or overly permissive security rules using supported Windows policy representations.

Name: Security Documentation Generator
Description: Automatically produce a readable report of all 79 layers, supported capabilities, enabled protections, limitations, and current configuration.

Name: Known-Malicious Domain Blocking
Description: Block validated high-confidence malicious domains when a safe Windows-compatible DNS or network enforcement method exists. Preserve legitimate system resolution and support observation before enforcement.

Name: Download and Temporary File Malware Scanning
Description: Scan new files in Downloads, temporary folders, and removable drives using appropriately integrated scanning capabilities. Apply quarantine only when detection confidence and file-recovery safeguards justify it.

Name: USB and Removable Device Alerts
Description: Notify when new storage and input devices appear. Never automatically block or disable essential keyboards, mice, or other input devices.

Name: Ransomware Behavior Monitoring
Description: Detect suspicious mass file changes, unusual renaming, and access to protected ransomware canary files. Alert by default, without aggressive automatic process termination.

Name: Beaconing Detection
Description: Analyze available network connection history for suspicious recurring outbound communications and other recognizable command-and-control beaconing indicators.
